findings.title: Frequency control writes a decile mid that is not on the frequency entity's step
findings.claim: On every heating state the compressor frequency write sends FrequencyMap's decile midpoint (23.5, 37.5, 51.5, 86.5 Hz) to a number entity whose step is 1 Hz, so the command lies off the entity's grid in 50 of 50 heating rows (10 states x 5 rigs).
findings.mechanism: coordinator._command_frequency sends round(target, 1) from freq_control.FrequencyMap.recommend, whose candidates are hz_min + (decile + 0.5) * span / 10; nothing puts the value on the entity's 'step' attribute, while every set-point write goes through inputs.write_setpoint, which does (setpoint_step). Home Assistant's number.set_value validates min/max only, so the off-step value reaches the device integration, which rounds, truncates or refuses it.

findings.title: A space-only step on a pump with no heating-only mode charges a cold tank: the DHW gate is floored at 30 C
findings.claim: With a mode select offering only Heating + DHW (GCHV), a step booking f kW of space heat and no hot water writes the tank set-point 30 C over a 20 C tank whose start hysteresis is 5 K, so the pump is asked to charge the tank on a step the plan booked none: 2 of 2 such rigs.
findings.mechanism: pump_arbiter.desired, space row with no Heating option: dhw_setpoint = _bounded(DHW_GATE_C=30, rounding down) — the entity's minimum but never below 30 C, independent of the tank reading; the hot-water entity in the rig accepts down to 10 C. A tank under 30 C less the pump's own hysteresis starts charging under Heating + DHW.

findings.title: A space boost on an indoor set-point entity holds the plan's partial set-point, not the band top
findings.claim: With Boost Space Heating live on a partial step and an indoor space set-point entity, the pump holds optimal_setpoints[K] = 21.0 C while the boost's own action asks max_temperature 23.0 C, on 2 of 2 indoor rigs; the water rigs write the top (55 C).
findings.mechanism: pump_arbiter.desired passes boosted only for a water unit ('The boost fact is read for a water set-point only'); _space_target's indoor branch reads _planned_room(result, now), the plan's step, while boost.overlay replaced the action's setpoint with max_temp. The boost lifts the supply switch and mode but never the indoor set-point, so the pump's own thermostat stops at the plan's partial target.

findings.title: A plan that goes stale on an idle step leaves the supply switch off: the pump is never handed back
findings.claim: When the last fresh actuation switched the pump off (an idle step) and solves then fail, the power switch still reads off 100 and 130 minutes past the plan's end on 5 of 5 rigs, and the arbiter writes nothing, so the pump is not handed back to its own thermostats; with the switch on at that moment the baseline row holds on 5 of 5.
findings.mechanism: coordinator._apply_action returns before the supply write once _plan_is_stale ('the pump's own weather-compensated curve holds comfort'), supply_tick's step_supply answers None on a stale plan, and pump_arbiter._pump_off stops every arbiter write while the switch reads off, so the baseline row (Heating + DHW, configured tank, hold flow) is never written either. Nothing switches the supply on until a solve succeeds.

findings.title: A mode write to an unavailable select is recorded as made
findings.claim: With the mode select, hot-water and space entities unavailable at a partial step's switch-on, the arbiter records the mode write in held.written (and reports it to duty_switch) although Home Assistant's entity service call skips an unavailable entity, on 5 of 5 rigs.
findings.mechanism: pump_arbiter._write gates on 'state is None', never on state 'unavailable'; _lead_mode writes the step's mode ahead of the switch-on, services.async_call returns without error because Home Assistant leaves an unavailable entity out of the call, and held.written, _report_write (duty_switch.note_mode_write) and _persist record a write that never landed. The stub FakeServices records every call, so the suite cannot see it. The pump then starts in its previous mode; the next pass after the entity returns rewrites it (hold), so the cost is one tick and a phantom mode switch in the learner.

leads.what: No _plan_is_stale gate, unlike _apply_action and _space_pump_to_drive: in cells.py's baseline-on run the stale action's 3.0 kW was asked of FrequencyMap.recommend 100 min past the plan; the last frequency is held and never handed back on stale, off or unload (D16.M6 restore).

partial entered from idle (cell 3530): the switch-on writes only the mode ahead; the space set-point follows at the next one-minute tick (cells.py timeline fork-flow partial: 07:02 mode + switch on, 07:03 space 44 C), so the pump starts against the idle gate (25 C) for up to a minute (D16.M3/M4).

D12 configuration level: on an install with no power switch the idle row leaves the mode as last written (often Heating + DHW after a baseline) and holds the configured tank set-point, so the tank thermostat may charge on idle steps; not measured here (the rigs all configure a switch).
D1 staleness neighbour of D16-s1-04: the plan-stale path and the supply switch; D1 owns whether the stale state is reached and announced.
